title: Reading a Randomised Trial — Bias, Confidence Intervals and What to Trust

hook.en: A headline says "treatment X works", but did the trial deserve our trust? Learn a simple way to read a randomised trial, spot the usual weaknesses and decide if the result matters for your patient.
hook.ur: Headline kehti hai "ilaj X kaam karta hai", magar kya trial hamare bharose ke laiq thi? Randomised trial parhne ka saada tareeqa, aam kamzoriyan pehchanna aur faisla karna seekhein ke nateeja aap ke mareez ke liye ahem hai ya nahi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll check a trial for random allocation, concealment, blinding, dropouts and outcome reporting, read a mean difference with its confidence interval, and decide whether the result is both believable and important.
goal.ur: End tak aap trial mein random allocation, concealment, blinding, dropouts aur outcome reporting check karenge, mean difference ko confidence interval ke saath parhenge, aur faisla karenge ke nateeja qabil-e-yaqeen bhi hai aur ahem bhi.

text.en: A **randomised controlled trial** compares groups made by chance, so the groups are alike except for the treatment. It is a strong design, but not all trials are equally trustworthy. Ask four questions: **Was allocation random and hidden? Were people and assessors blinded where possible? Did most people finish and get analysed as allocated? Was the main outcome reported as planned?** Then ask the practical question: **how big is the effect, and is it important to patients?**
text.ur: **Randomised controlled trial** aise groups ka muqabla karta hai jo ittefaq se bane, is liye groups ilaj ke ilawa ek jaise hote hain. Yeh mazboot design hai, magar har trial barabar qabil-e-bharosa nahi. Chaar sawal poochhein: **Kya allocation random aur chhupa hua tha? Kya log aur assessors jahan mumkin ho blinded thay? Kya zyada tar log mukammal hue aur allocation ke mutabiq analyse hue? Kya mukhya nateeja plan ke mutabiq report hua?** Phir amali sawal poochhein: **asar kitna bara hai, aur kya mareezon ke liye ahem hai?**

text.en: Think of a trial as a **fair race**. Fair means the runners were drawn at random, nobody knew which lane the favourite had, the stopwatch operator did not know who was whom, and runners who dropped out were counted. If any of these is missing, a "winner" may reflect the unfair race, not the better runner.
text.ur: Trial ko **munsifana daud** samjhein. Munsifana ka matlab hai daudne walay ittefaq se chune gaye, kisi ko nahi pata tha ke pasandeeda ki lane kaun si hai, stopwatch chalane wale ko maloom nahi tha kaun kaun hai, aur jo daud chhor gaye unhein ginti mein rakha gaya. In mein se kuch kam ho to "jeetne wala" daud ki be-insafi dikha sakta hai, behtar daudne wale ko nahi.

steps.title: Check how groups were formed
steps.detail: Was the sequence truly random (computer, not alternation) and hidden from the people enrolling patients? If not, the groups may differ from the start. || Dekhein groups kaise bane

steps.title: Check blinding and follow-up
steps.detail: Patients cannot always be blinded in exercise trials, but assessors often can. Look at how many were lost in each group; large or uneven losses can distort results. || Blinding aur follow-up dekhein

steps.title: Read the effect size
steps.detail: Look for the difference between groups in a measure you understand, with its **95 percent confidence interval**. The interval shows the range of values compatible with the data. || Asar ka size parhein

steps.title: Judge importance and fit
steps.detail: Compare the difference with the minimal important change for that outcome, and ask if your patient resembles those studied and if the treatment is available and safe. || Ahmiyat aur munasibat parkhein

question.en: Which feature makes a trial's randomisation more trustworthy?
question.ur: Kaun si khaasiyat trial ki randomisation ko zyada qabil-e-bharosa banati hai?

feedback.ur: Agla group peshgoi ke qabil hai.

text.en: A computer-generated sequence hidden from those enrolling patients
text.ur: Computer se bana sequence jo mareez daakhil karne walon se chhupa ho

feedback.ur: Haan — yeh selection bias se bachata hai.

text.en: Giving treatment to patients who ask for it

rows.en: Is the result unlikely to be due to chance alone?
rows.ur: Kya nateeja sirf ittefaq se hona kam mumkin hai?

rows.en: Is the change large enough to matter to a patient?
rows.ur: Kya tabdeeli itni bari hai ke mareez ke liye ahem ho?

rows.en: Sample size and spread of data
rows.ur: Sample size aur data ka phailao

rows.en: The size of the effect against a patient-based threshold
rows.ur: Mareez par mabni hadd ke muqable mein asar ka size

rows.en: A very large trial can find a tiny, useless difference
rows.ur: Bahut bara trial chhota, bekaar farq dhoondh sakta hai

rows.en: A small trial can miss a real, important difference
rows.ur: Chhota trial asli, ahem farq miss kar sakta hai

rows.en: The p-value and the confidence interval
The effect against the minimal important change
rows.ur: Asar ko minimal important change ke muqable mein

text.en: **Fair, finished, found, fits.** Fair groups, finished follow-up, found an effect big enough to matter, and a result that fits your patient. Miss one, and trust a little less.
text.ur: **Munsifana, mukammal, mila, fit.** Munsifana groups, mukammal follow-up, itna bara asar jo ahem ho, aur nateeja jo aap ke mareez par fit ho. Ek kam ho to bharosa thora kam karein.

text.en: **Stopping at the p-value.** A p-value below 0.05 does not tell you how large or important the effect is, and one above 0.05 does not show there is no effect. Always read the difference and its confidence interval.
text.ur: **p-value par ruk jana.** 0.05 se kam p-value yeh nahi batati ke asar kitna bara ya ahem hai, aur 0.05 se zyada ka matlab yeh nahi ke asar nahi. Hamesha farq aur uska confidence interval parhein.

question.en: A trial reports a 1-point difference in pain on a 0 to 10 scale, 95 percent CI 0.3 to 1.7, p = 0.006. What is the best interpretation?
question.ur: Trial 0 se 10 ke scale par dard mein 1 point ka farq batati hai, 95 percent CI 0.3 se 1.7, p = 0.006. Behtareen tabeer kya hai?

text.en: The treatment clearly works well for patients
text.ur: Ilaj mareezon ke liye saaf taur par achha kaam karta hai

feedback.en: The effect is under the usual important change.
feedback.ur: Asar aam ahem tabdeeli se kam hai.

text.en: The effect is probably real but may be too small to matter, since the usual important change is about 2 points
text.ur: Asar shayad asli hai magar itna chhota ho sakta hai ke ahem na ho, kyunke aam ahem tabdeeli takreeban 2 points hai

feedback.en: Yes — compare the whole interval with the minimal important change.
feedback.ur: Haan — poore interval ko minimal important change se milayein.

text.en: There is no effect because the difference is small
text.ur: Farq chhota hone se koi asar nahi

feedback.en: The interval shows a real, if small, effect.
feedback.ur: Interval asli, chhota hi sahi, asar dikhata hai.

question.en: What does a wide confidence interval tell you?
question.ur: Chauda confidence interval aap ko kya batata hai?

feedback.en: Width is about precision, not size.
feedback.ur: Chaurai durustgi ke baare mein hai, size ke nahi.

text.en: The estimate is imprecise, often from a small study
text.ur: Andaza ghair durust hai, aksar chhoti study ki wajah se

feedback.en: Yes — a wide interval means uncertainty.
feedback.ur: Haan — chauda interval ghair yaqeeni dikhata hai.

text.en: **Ask three questions before you change practice.** Is it trustworthy? Is the effect big enough to matter? Does it fit my patient and setting? A single trial rarely settles a question; look for systematic reviews and guidelines too. Keep a note of the papers you use and why.
text.ur: **Practice badalne se pehle teen sawal poochhein.** Kya yeh qabil-e-bharosa hai? Kya asar itna bara hai ke ahem ho? Kya yeh mere mareez aur setting par fit hai? Ek trial shayad hi sawal hal kare; systematic reviews aur guidelines bhi dekhein. Jin papers ko istemal karein un ka note aur wajah likhein.

question.en: Why is concealment of allocation different from blinding?
question.ur: Allocation ki concealment blinding se alag kyun hai?

answer.en: Concealment protects the moment of assigning people to groups: the person enrolling patients cannot know or influence which group is next. Blinding protects the period after assignment: patients, therapists and assessors do not know who has which treatment, so expectations cannot change care or measurement.
answer.ur: Concealment woh lamha bachati hai jab logon ko groups mein daala jata hai: mareez daakhil karne wala nahi jaan sakta ya asar daal sakta ke agla group kaun sa hai. Blinding assignment ke baad ka daur bachata hai: mareez, therapists aur assessors nahi jaante ke kis ko kaun sa ilaj mila, is liye tawaqqaat care ya paimaish badal nahi sakti.

beats.patient: A trial of a new manual technique for neck pain reports an average pain reduction of 1.2 points versus placebo (95 percent CI 0.2 to 2.2). Allocation was random and hidden, assessors were blinded, but 30 percent of one group were lost to follow-up and the trial had 60 people.
beats.assessment: The effect is small, the interval is wide and spans trivial to important change, and the losses may bias the result.
beats.treatment: Describe the finding as a possible small benefit, look for other trials or a review and weigh it with safety, cost and patient preference.
beats.reassess: You decide to offer it as an option, explain the uncertainty and track the patient's own results.

text.en: **Never stop or change a patient's care from one paper alone.** For anything involving safety, medicines or red flags, use guidelines and the medical team. If an article claims dramatic benefit from a simple treatment, check the source, conflicts of interest and whether the result has been repeated.
text.ur: **Sirf ek paper par mareez ki care na roken ya badlein.** Hifazat, dawaiyon ya red flags ke mamlay mein guidelines aur medical team istemal karein. Agar koi article saade ilaj ka dramatic faida batae to source, mufaadat ka takrao aur kya nateeja dohraya gaya hai check karein.

summary.en: Check how groups were formed (random and hidden), blinding and follow-up, and whether the main outcome was reported as planned.
summary.ur: Dekhein groups kaise bane (random aur chhupa hua), blinding aur follow-up, aur kya mukhya nateeja plan ke mutabiq report hua.

summary.en: Read the difference between groups and its 95 percent confidence interval, not only the p-value.
summary.ur: Groups ka farq aur uska 95 percent confidence interval parhein, sirf p-value nahi.

summary.en: Judge whether the effect is important by comparing it with the minimal important change, and whether it fits your patient.
summary.ur: Asar ki ahmiyat ko minimal important change se milakar parkhein, aur dekhein ke kya yeh aap ke mareez par fit hai.

back.en: Makes groups alike by chance, apart from the treatment.
back.ur: Groups ko ilaj ke ilawa ittefaq se ek jaisa banati hai.

front.en: What does a 95 percent confidence interval show?
front.ur: 95 percent confidence interval kya dikhata hai?

back.en: The range of effect sizes compatible with the data.
back.ur: Asar ke woh sizes jo data ke mutabiq hain.

front.en: What is the difference between statistical and clinical importance?
front.ur: Statistical aur clinical ahmiyat mein kya farq hai?

back.en: Statistical means unlikely by chance; clinical means large enough to matter to patients.
back.ur: Statistical ka matlab ittefaq se kam mumkin; clinical ka matlab mareezon ke liye ahem hone ke qabil bara.
Tawaqqaat ka care ya paimaish badalna.
